content_units: Best Laptop Match for a Business School Student

For your priorities—  battery life first, portability second, light photo editing third, and staying under $1,300  —  Laptop A is the best overall fit  . It aligns most closely with daily campus use: long classes, library work, commuting, and general productivity without carrying extra weight or worrying about charging.
Laptop-by-Laptop Comparison
Laptop   Price   Weight   Battery   RAM / Storage   Graphics   Best For
Laptop A     $1,249       1.24 kg       18 hrs     16GB / 512GB   Integrated   Best all-around student choice
Laptop B     $1,299     1.46 kg   10 hrs   16GB / 1TB   Entry-level dedicated   Better if photo editing matters more
Laptop C     $999     1.8 kg   12 hrs   8GB / 512GB   Integrated   Budget pick, but weaker long-term value
Ranked Recommendation
Option 1:   Laptop A     Best balance of battery life, portability, and enough performance for schoolwork plus light photo editing     Top overall fit
Pros
- Excellent   18-hour battery life
- Lightest option at   1.24 kg
-   16GB RAM   is strong for multitasking, research tabs, Office apps, Zoom, and light editing
- Stays under budget with room for accessories
- 13.6-inch size is very travel-friendly
Cons
- Only   512GB storage
- Integrated graphics is fine for light editing, but not ideal for heavier creative work
- Smaller screen may feel a bit tighter for editing spreadsheets and photos
Option 2:   Laptop B     Strong second choice if you want more storage and somewhat better editing capability     Best creative-leaning alternative
Pros
-   1TB SSD   gives much more room for files, photos, and apps
- Dedicated entry-level graphics may help in some photo-editing workflows
-   16GB RAM   is still solid
- 14-inch display offers a nice middle ground between portability and workspace
Cons
- Battery life drops to   10 hours  , a major downside for all-day campus use
- Heavier than Laptop A
- Uses your full budget at   $1,299
- Performance gain for light photo editing may not be worth the battery trade-off
Option 3:   Laptop C     Cheapest option, but it gives up too much in memory and portability for your use case     Budget-first choice
Pros
- Lowest price at   $999
- 15.6-inch display is nice for spreadsheets and side-by-side work
- Decent battery on paper at   12 hours
Cons
- Only   8GB RAM  , which is the biggest weakness here
- Heaviest option at   1.8 kg
- Large size is less convenient for commuting and class
- Integrated graphics plus lower RAM make it less appealing for editing and long-term multitasking
Final Pick: Laptop A
Why Laptop A wins
- It best matches your stated priorities in order:
-   Battery life:   clearly the strongest
-   Portability:   also the best
-   Light photo editing:   16GB RAM makes it capable enough
-   Budget:   comfortably under the cap
Who should choose Laptop B instead
- Pick B only if you care enough about   extra storage   and a bit more graphics help to accept much shorter battery life.
Who should choose Laptop C instead
- Pick C only if minimizing upfront cost matters more than long-term convenience and performance.
Buying Context
I’m assuming:
- “Light photo editing” means tasks like Lightroom basics, Photoshop touch-ups, Canva, or similar—not heavy professional editing.
- Business school use includes note-taking, browser-heavy multitasking, Office/Sheets, presentations, video calls, and portability across campus.
